clues: This town sits in the Chocó part of Colombia. It lies in the far west of South America.
This place may get more rain than almost any place on Earth. Its yearly rain adds up to about 12,717 mm.
This town took its name from Gioró. He was a chief here before Columbus reached the Americas.
This place claims a world rain record. Yet the official top spot sits far away in India.
From 1952 to 1989, workers at its farm wrote down the wet weather. A Bogotá university ran that farm.
